answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small refundable deposit that only unlocks after a history of useful work, like a vine that must root before it can climb. Verification is quartz-clear: peers audit past transactions and slash deposits of agents caught duplicating identities. Each fake identity then costs real capital and time, so a ripple of cheap clones cannot flood the market; an attacker must fund every clone separately, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
